commitResults.messageTitle: Updated Dingleberry.java to greet and exit
commitResults.messageBody: Added horizontal lines and greeting message to main java file
Changed Dingleberry into command-line app. Reads user input, echoes each line, exits when the user types "bye".
Added function to save up to 100 tasks. Input goes into a str[] and list iterates all list items
Used constants for max tasks and seperator
Allows 2 new commands, mark and unmark and formats such that the done state is visible.

ToDos: tasks without any date/time attached to them, e.g., visit new theme park
Deadlines: tasks that need to be done before a specific date/time, e.g., submit report by 11/10/2019 5pm
Events: tasks that start at a specific date/time and end at a specific date/time,
e.g., (a) team project meeting 2/10/2019 2-4pm (b) orientation week 4/10/2019 to 11/10/2019

commitResults.messageTitle: Chat supports todo, deadline, and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody: This change adds parsing for todo, deadline, and event commands, creating the appropriate task types and printing the expected task-added confirmation messages. It also fixes the task type formatting so the brackets are displayed without an extra space before the task status.
Exception handling for Incorrect chat response

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI test runner and refactor Dingleberry
commitResults.messageBody: Add a PowerShell-based console UI test runner and test plan, plus documentation for the test skill. Files added: .github/skills/test-ui/SKILL.md, .github/skills/test-ui/scripts/run-ui-tests.ps1, and test/ui-test-plan.md. Refactor src/main/java/Dingleberry.java to improve input validation, normalize the input loop (reads until EOF or MAX_TASKS), add helper methods (ensureCapacity, requireValue, printAddedTask), and centralize error handling via DingleberryException with clearer user-facing messages. Changes make command behavior deterministic for automated UI tests (unsupported commands now produce explicit error messages).
Delete function added + updated the list to Java Collections ArrayList<Task> instead
Used enums to consolidate commands to simplify code
